core_idea: Alone means with no other person there, or with no one and nothing else involved.

senses.definition: without any other person with you

examples.text: Kim lives alone in a small apartment near the station.
I don't like walking home alone at night.
Are you alone, or is someone with you?
When the guests had gone, we were finally alone.

compare.note: lonely says that you are unhappy because you have no company; alone says only that no one else is there

adaptation.semantic: Alone here is a plain fact with no feeling attached; do not translate it with a word that suggests sadness.

senses.definition: without anyone to help or support you, or feeling that no one shares your situation

examples.text: You're not alone; a lot of people find this hard.
examples.note: you are not the only one

examples.text: After the argument she felt completely alone.
He was left alone to deal with the problem.

items: be left alone to do something

senses.definition: being the only one; and no one or nothing else

examples.text: Sara alone knew where the key was.
The rent alone costs more than I earn in a month.
Talent alone is not enough; you also have to work.
Time alone will tell whether the plan works.

adaptation.semantic: This is the word only placed after the noun; most languages translate it with their ordinary word for only, in its usual position.

word_family.note: only before a noun: a lone tree

synonym_discrimination.note: Alone says only that no one else is there, and carries no feeling: Kim lives alone and likes it. Lonely says that you are unhappy because you have no company, and you can be lonely in a crowd: He felt lonely in the new city. On your own means the same as alone and is more common in speech; it also means without help: I fixed it on my own.

usage_note: Alone is also used as an adverb, with the same meaning: She traveled alone. I did it alone. Leave me alone (stop bothering me) is under leave, and let alone (even less) is under let.

learner_errors.note: Lonely means sad because you have no company; alone is neutral.
Alone never comes before a noun; use on her own, or single if you mean not married.
Alone takes no preposition; by goes with myself: by myself.

etymology.text: Alone is all plus one: it began as the phrase all one, meaning wholly by yourself. Lone was made from it later by dropping the first syllable, and lonely comes from lone.

adaptation.semantic: Many languages have one word for alone and lonely; English separates the plain fact (alone) from the unhappy feeling (lonely). The only sense (Sara alone) is a different word in most languages.
adaptation.grammar: Alone never comes before a noun: it follows be, feel, live, or leave, or, in the only sense, follows the noun itself: the cost alone. It takes no preposition.
adaptation.pronunciation: Two syllables with the stress on the second; the first vowel is the weak ə, as in about.
